findings.title: [P1] Keep branch names out of the shell
findings.body: When `branch` is caller-controlled, values such as `HEAD; id` are interpreted as shell syntax and execute an additional command with the application's privileges. The previous `execFile` call passed the branch as one literal Git argument; preserve that argument-vector invocation instead of interpolating it into `exec`.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve cancellation of the actual Git process
findings.body: If callers cancel a slow or large `git show` via the returned child's `kill()`, `exec` targets the intermediate shell and can leave its Git child running with inherited streams. The previous `execFile` return value represented Git directly, so this change regresses cancellation and may leave work consuming resources after cancellation.
